title: Document Extraction Guides | PageSignal
description: Practical guides to converting PDFs and scanned images into reviewed JSON, plus native React, Angular and Vue integration with PageSignal.
heading: Document extraction guides
body:
Understand how to turn PDFs and scanned images into structured data, verify the results, and connect a document workspace to your application.

WORKFLOW GUIDE

Convert PDFs and scans to JSON

Choose a readable document, identify its type, extract fields, ask follow-up questions, and review the output before exporting.

DEVELOPER GUIDE

React, Angular, Vue, API and SDK

Choose the right package, understand the backend adapter, and keep model credentials on the server.

Choose a workflow

The web workspace is the quickest way to try document review. Developers can use the API documentation to run their own processing service, or add native framework components to an existing application. Consult release notes before upgrading a package.

Review is part of extraction

AI can misread handwriting, damaged scans, ambiguous dates and complex tables. Keep the source available, check important values, and preserve missing values rather than filling them with guesses. These guides explain the current capabilities and limitations rather than promising perfect results.

title: Convert PDFs and Scanned Documents to JSON | PageSignal Guide
description: Learn to upload PDFs and scans, identify document types with AI, extract fields, verify source evidence and export structured JSON using PageSignal.
heading: How to convert PDFs and scanned documents to JSON
body:
A document is easy to read but often difficult to use in software. PageSignal provides an open-source workspace for identifying document types, extracting information, reviewing it alongside the source, and exporting JSON.

1. Start with a readable PDF or image

Open the PageSignal workspace and sign in with a configured provider. Drag files into the upload area or choose Browse files. Supported formats are PDF, PNG, JPEG, WebP and BMP. A batch can contain up to 10 files, with a 30 MiB limit per file and a 100 MiB combined limit. PDFs can contain up to 40 pages. These are application limits, not a statement of the AI provider’s maximum limits.

A PDF may already contain a text layer. A scanned PDF or image needs optical character recognition (OCR). Local OCR currently uses English recognition. Clear, upright pages with readable text produce a better starting point; low-resolution photos, shadows, handwriting and overlapping marks can reduce accuracy.

2. Identify the document and extract information

Use the primary AI action in Extraction review, or enable AI extraction before uploading. Review the confirmation before sending page images and extracted text to the configured AI service. The application can process multiple documents in a bounded queue; you do not need to start each one separately.

Document identification is open vocabulary: it is not restricted to a fixed list of industries or forms. The AI attempts to identify a document’s title, type, issuer and form details where visible. Ambiguous or unreadable content can remain unknown or require review. A file containing distinct forms may be reported as mixed documents.

3. Review the fields against the original

The review workspace places fields beside the source preview. Select a field or citation to navigate to its page and locate supporting text when a reliable match exists. Inspect repeated labels, dates, identifiers, checkboxes and table rows carefully. A matching label is not proof that the value has been read correctly.

Correct errors before exporting. Missing or illegible information should remain empty or null rather than becoming a plausible guess. Precise highlighting depends on available PDF text or OCR positions; a poor scan may support page navigation without an exact highlight.

4. Ask for specific information

If you need selected values, enter the labels in Find specific fields. For example: “Find the reference number, issue date and total amount.” Use Ask for a follow-up question about the document. The current query flow searches supplied numbered page text and successful extracted field information; it does not independently reread the original images. Run vision extraction first when OCR is unclear, and verify the returned evidence.

5. Export structured JSON

Export the selected document after reviewing its values. The web export includes schema version, fields, evidence and source metadata, with additional page and classification information for AI results. It differs from a single-page API response. The abbreviated example below illustrates common properties; see the output format documentation for details.

{
  "schema_version": "3.0",
  "document_type": "application_form",
  "fields": {
    "reference_number": "REF-2048",
    "renewal_date": null
  }
}

What happens to uploaded documents?

The current workspace holds uploads, edits and conversations in the browser tab rather than a durable document library. Export before refreshing or closing it. With AI enabled, page images, text and relevant query context pass through the server to the provider. Review the privacy notice and use a suitable deployment for your information.

For an embedded workflow, read the package integration guide. Source code is available on GitHub; self-hosting requires your own model credentials and hosting.

title: Document Extraction for React, Angular & Vue | PageSignal Packages
description: Choose PageSignal’s native React, Angular or Vue document workspace, Node.js extraction core or HTTP SDK. Learn what each package includes and how adapters work.
heading: Integrate document extraction into your application
body:
PageSignal offers native document workspaces for React, Angular and Vue, plus server-side extraction libraries. Choose the interface that fits your application rather than embedding the hosted website in an iframe.

Choose your package

PackagePurposeRuns in
@pagesignal/reactNative workspace for React 18 and 19Browser
@pagesignal/angularStandalone Angular 21 workspaceBrowser
@pagesignal/vueNative Vue 3.5 workspaceBrowser
@pagesignal/coreCall the extraction engine with your provider keyNode.js server
@pagesignal/sdkCall a self-hosted PageSignal serviceNode.js server

What the native workspace provides

The framework components provide drag-and-drop upload, multiple-file queue management, bounded parallel processing, progress and error states, editable fields, document previews, query controls and JSON download. The state controller is shared through the browser-safe SDK workspace entry point. Each framework renders its own DOM.

Provide an adapter with an asynchronous extract function and, optionally, a query function. The adapter connects the component to your application’s backend. It must honor AbortSignal to stop upstream work when a document is removed or processing is cancelled. See the adapter contract and examples.

What you still implement

The UI packages do not bundle AI extraction, OCR, PDF rasterization, account login or a backend. Native PDF preview uses the browser’s PDF viewer; precise source overlays and richer page controls in the hosted application are not included in these initial components. Be explicit about these boundaries when planning an integration.

Your backend validates uploads, authenticates users, enforces size and cost limits, renders pages as needed, and calls your chosen extraction service. Keep OpenAI and PageSignal service keys on the server. Never include a service credential in a browser bundle.

Choose direct extraction or an HTTP service

Use the core package to call the engine from Node.js without running a separate PageSignal HTTP service. Use the SDK when your backend needs to call a self-hosted Community server. Both currently extract a rendered JPEG page or query caller-supplied numbered page text; neither accepts a PDF binary directly. Your application supplies PDF parsing and multi-page orchestration.

The hosted website uses account sessions, while Community service examples use a service key. Do not assume a hosted login session or the website’s allowance is an npm package API key. The authentication documentation explains these deployment modes.

Start with a complete example

Follow the framework-specific examples in the React, Angular or Vue documentation. Keep configuration stable where required by each component’s lifecycle, validate the returned schema, and review extracted values before passing them into a business workflow.

Open source and versioning

The repository and packages are MIT licensed. You can inspect and adapt the implementation while preserving required notices; model usage and hosting remain separate costs. React v2 replaces the earlier iframe props with an adapter API. Review release history and migration notes before upgrading, and report reproducible integration issues on GitHub.
